correctness.rationale: The inverse and force preserve each rational denominator grid modulo 2, so the quotient orbit returns. The lifted block displacement is the geometric sum of the R^n rotations of the first displacement; for 4 not dividing n this sum vanishes over the order of R^n, and for 4 dividing n it grows linearly unless v=0. This gives exactly the phase formula and radial, not vector, speed. Independently set m=N/2 and e2=(0,1). During the first B-run the homogeneous reference inputs B^j A(t+h,t-h) have vertical coordinates strictly in (-1,0); during the second B-run the homogeneous reference inputs -B^j B^m A(t+h,t-h) have vertical coordinates strictly in (1,2), for 0<=j<m. At the two intermediate A steps and the last one the residue is strictly in (0,1). In units of the lattice spacing 2, the first B-run accumulates u=sum_{j=0}^{m-1}R^j e2; the second run starts at shift -u and adds -e2 each step after lattice rotation. The total shift after the last A is -R(I+R^m)u. The homogeneous product M_N=-AB^N A sends each input on S_N to z+(2,-2) and is the derivative there. The correction is zero for m even and (-2,2) in planar units for m odd, so the exact parity return holds for all real h in the open segment. Lattice covariance repeats the accelerating block (R^(N+4)=I), and the period in the segment claim need not be least. The force jumps at even seams in the plane; only its quotient is asserted continuous. The supplied rational checker was inspected, not executed; the independent derivation covers the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The exact segment calculation distinguishes true linear transport from bounded motion in an existing example where finite tracking alone could not do so. It gives an infinite family of nonzero speeds accumulating at zero, including irrational starts on the specified segments, and a neutral derivative explaining the parabolic geometry. It asserts neither positive area nor typical diffusion.
